text: Faerah is a servant of Eilistraee.
Faerah's sister may have survived and escaped the Underdark.
Redgrave carries the soul of a member of the Order of the Silver Dragon.
Yevelda's parents died defending Barovia.
The Trickster God is Roark Battleborn's father.
Bound by the gods' ancient non-interference compact, the Trickster God seeks Roark Battleborn's help as his mortal agent.
Wisp's master is a member of the Eternal Watch, and fell into a coma the instant Vecna's escape broke the ward he maintained.

The Silent Ascendency buys stolen magic items, and targets the party's own magical power, to drain them into soul-vessels built from stolen fragments of Eludrax's soul-craft and feed the energy to Vecna's ascension.
Eludrax's soul-craft is the same craft that fed the original seal binding Vecna and produced Redgrave's bound soul.
The Silent Ascendency has been draining stolen magic items to fuel a ritual.
The gem can hold a creature's essence, and it held Roark Battleborn's.
Anastrasya survived Strahd's wedding-night battle and fled, and Vecna's forces are courting her.
Donavich's son is a vampire spawn, and the screams beneath the church are his.
Once freed, Emil returned to the werewolf pack and took control of it.
Hesper Crane's ledger named the network's next contact in Duskferry, known only as 'the Tallyman.'
Strahd wants Ireena and has bitten her twice.
Ireena's adoptive father had just died, and she wanted him buried before she left.
Izek survived the fall of Castle Ravenloft and was claimed by Vecna's power in that moment; the party freed him from Vecna's control (S49).
The Silent Ascendency captured Velmont and took over his magic-item smuggling operation.
Madam Eva knows things about the party's pasts that she has no ordinary way of knowing.
Marrow carries a soul-graft, the Marrow-rite, built from the same Eludrax soul-craft as the Amber Wardens, which lets it borrow a disguise target's trained reflexes and muscle memory.
The ambush on Roark and Lyssandra was opportunistic: the Ascendency had no advance knowledge of Corwin Vantor's detection device.
Marrow was the Silent Ascendency's cell leader in Bruokdon.
Marrow captured and impersonated Lord Caldris Velmont, then Professor Gousse Windcaller, and escaped into a crowd when Faerah saw through it.
Marrow took Roark Battleborn's identity; Faerah saw through it and killed Marrow in single combat.
The dwarf's confession to leading the Bruokdon cell was a lie.
Ostwin Reyes is the Tallyman, the Silent Ascendency's contact in Duskferry.
Strahd poses as the nobleman Vasili von Holtz.
Vecna's end goal is to become the God of Truth and dominate reality.
Redgrave's killing blow on Strahd drew out Strahd's soul, and that was the final piece that freed Vecna from the Amber Temple.
Vecna's ascension takes two rituals: the World-Truth Working creates a vacant Truth-domain and stakes his claim to it through a built-in exception, and the Ascension Rite executes that claim.
Vecna's claim on the Truth-domain is dishonestly won, so a genuinely total, unhedged claimant could override it at the Rite.
The cultists who lived in Death House revered Strahd.
Rose and Thorn were locked in the attic of Death House, and their remains were found there.
The ghosts of Carl and Elisabeth, the house's previous owners, haunt Death House.

text: The bones of St. Andral protected the church from Barovia's evil until they were stolen from its crypt.
Thornmere was only a small-scale prototype of Vecna's truth-magic, not the Working itself.
A wizard once gathered the townsfolk to rise against Strahd.
